PAPERS.short: Kutarna SWAPIT Toronto winter NO2 O3 PM2.5 AQHI representativeness 2026
PAPERS.title: Insights into urban concentrations and variability of NO(2), O(3), and PM(2.5) from the study of winter air pollution in Toronto (SWAPIT).
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 with NO2 and O3 at eight continuous sites, plus NAPS history from 1997
PAPERS.affil: Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canada; Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canada
PAPERS.n: Eight continuous sites across Toronto, six weeks January-March 2024, plus NAPS records from 1997. The published community AQHI, built from four NAPS stations, deviated by more than 2 AQHI units above and below values at other sites. NO2 dominated short-term AQHI risk and rose under calm winds; O3 rose with wind speed; PM2.5 showed local and regional features. Median AQHI fell almost twice as fast in summer as in winter, leaving winter higher since 2013. No CI. Limitation: one six-week winter at eight sites, and the abstract names neither instrument class nor site typology, so the deviation cannot be assigned to siting or to method. Relevance: high - a quantified gap between a four-station index and the intra-urban field, the case for denser sensing, though NO2 rather than PM2.5 drives it.

PAPERS.short: Stegmann atmospheric aging biomass burning particle toxicity BEAS-2B PHOTO-LAC 2026
PAPERS.title: Atmospheric Aging Modifies the Toxicological Profile of Biomass Burning Particles in Epithelial Lung Cells.
PAPERS.pm: Fresh vs chamber-aged biomass burning particle extracts, flaming and smoldering
PAPERS.endpoint: ROS, oxidative DNA damage, transcriptome, inflammatory and matrix protein expression
PAPERS.affil: Technical University of Munich, Germany; Technical University of Munich, Germany
PAPERS.n: Biomass burning particles from controlled flaming and smoldering combustion were aged in the PHOTO-LAC chamber under alternating photochemical and dark conditions, then extracts dosed on BEAS-2B bronchial cells. Aging enhanced intracellular ROS and oxidative DNA damage, most for smoldering emissions, with cytotoxicity largely unchanged. Inflammatory and matrix-remodelling responses were attenuated with aging in smoldering particles and stable in flaming particles. No fold-changes or doses in the abstract. Limitation: extracts on a submerged immortalised line, not air-liquid interface deposition, and one chamber aging protocol, so dose relevance to ambient plumes is open. Relevance: moderate - mass from a sensor is blind to aging state; a plume reading the same ug/m3 near source and downwind need not be the same exposure.

PAPERS.short: Park micro-3D-printed liquid-metal coil inductive ferrous aerosol impactor sensor 2026
PAPERS.title: Micro-3D-printed integrated system with liquid-metal coils for simultaneous size-selective sampling and concentration sensing of respirable ferrous metal aerosols.
PAPERS.pm: Respirable ferrous aerosol, 1-5 and >5 um fractions, inductive detection
PAPERS.endpoint: Cut-off diameters, calibration R2, concentration nRMSE
PAPERS.affil: Yonsei University, South Korea; Yonsei University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Monolithic micro-3D-printed platform: two-stage inertial impactor (aerodynamic cut-offs 5.28 and 0.99 um), aqueous particle transfer, 100 um sensing channels, embedded EGaIn solenoids (50 turns, 907.1 nH, maximum Q 9.1 at 30 MHz). Fe-only aerosol: peak-rate calibration R2 0.900 and 0.910, time-resolved nRMSE 6.72% and 8.95% for the two fractions. Arizona test dust background: R2 0.9428 and 0.9348 against APS total particle increments. Responses persisted over a 60-min mixed-aerosol challenge. Limitation: laboratory-generated aerosol only, no field, humidity, drift or unit-to-unit data, and the dust-background R2 is against total count, not ferrous mass. Relevance: moderate - composition-selective inductive sensing is an orthogonal channel to optical scattering, but far from a deployable node.

PAPERS.short: Borgini e-cigarette real-life indoor PM AirBeam3 bar traffic walk pilot 2026
PAPERS.title: Investigating the Real-Life Indoor Air Quality Impact of E-Cigarette Vaping.
PAPERS.pm: PM1, PM2.5, PM10 by portable optical particle counter (AirBeam3)
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor PM during vaping vs street microenvironments
PAPERS.affil: Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori, Italy; Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori, Italy
PAPERS.n: Pilot walk with an AirBeam3 along low- and heavy-traffic roads, then inside a bar with three people vaping. Bar PM2.5 averaged 28.8 ug/m3 with a peak of 84.7 ug/m3, 6.5 times the low-traffic and 3.1 times the heavy-traffic street value. No CI; a single session is implied, with no replicate or vape-free control in the same room. Limitation: e-cigarette aerosol is volatile liquid droplets, outside an ambient-dust factory calibration, and no gravimetric or reference co-location is reported, so the mass values are nominal; bar sources other than vaping are uncontrolled. Relevance: direct - a low-cost optical sensor reporting a mass ratio in an aerosol regime it was never characterised for. Read it as a relative signal.

PAPERS.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
PAPERS.short: Sharon IoT vape detection school PM2.5 PM10 37 locations 18 months 2026
PAPERS.title: Smart Vape Detection in Schools for Mitigating Student E-Cigarette Use
PAPERS.design: Longitudinal case study of a sensor deployment
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and PM10 at one-minute resolution, threshold alerting
PAPERS.endpoint: Vaping alert events, CCTV verification, staff response
PAPERS.affil: Blue IoT Pty Ltd, Australia; Queensland University of Technology, Australia
PAPERS.n: BACKFILL (entry 4 May 2026). Low-cost IoT PM nodes at 37 restroom and change-room locations in one Australian independent school, one-minute data for 18 months, threshold alerts with school-led CCTV verification. More than 300 vaping-related incidents, clustered by time of day and among senior students; alerts showed rapid concurrent PM2.5 and PM10 excursions. Staff response declined through alert fatigue, and a regional smoke event produced false positives. No sensitivity, specificity or denominator of unverified alerts in the abstract. Limitation: first-author affiliation is the IoT vendor; 'highly effective' is claimed without a confusion matrix. Relevance: high - event detection from PM transients on low-cost nodes, with the human-response failure and the need for context-aware logic documented.

PAPERS.short: Dyer urban burden of disease 825 European cities joint PM2.5 NO2 green space 2026
PAPERS.title: Urban burden of disease estimation for policy making: health impacts of environmental stressors
PAPERS.pm: Modelled PM2.5 and NO2, joint exposure estimation, against WHO guidelines
PAPERS.endpoint: Deaths attributable to exposure above WHO guidelines and to insufficient green space
PAPERS.affil: Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), Spain; not stated in Crossref
PAPERS.n: BACKFILL (Crossref deposit 26 October 2026; congress abstract). Comparative risk assessment across 825 European cities, three reporting periods 2015-2024. Exceeding WHO guidelines gave 213,889 deaths (95% CI 89,224-344,223) jointly attributable to PM2.5 and NO2 in 2018, reported as 76,833 fewer than summing single-pollutant estimates (PM2.5 145,747; NO2 143,646; the printed figures actually differ by 75,504). Limitation: abstract only; the joint method is not specified, the interval is wide, and attribution inherits the concentration-response function and the exposure model with no measured validation stated. Relevance: moderate - summing pollutant burdens overstates by about a quarter here, and city-scale burden accounting is where dense sensor fields could test the modelled surface.

PAPERS.short: Kim prenatal PM2.5 pediatric inguinal hernia hydrocele kriging cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Prenatal Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Exposure and the Risk of Pediatric Inguinal Hernia or Hydrocele: A Retrospective Cohort Study
PAPERS.pm: Monthly residential PM2.5 by kriging from fixed monitoring stations
PAPERS.affil: Keimyung University, South Korea; Keimyung University School of Medicine, South Korea
PAPERS.n: BACKFILL (entry 4 May 2026). 1,093 mother-offspring pairs, one tertiary centre, deliveries July 2016-June 2019, follow-up to March 2024; 53 cases (4.85%). Second-trimester PM2.5 OR 1.07 (1.01-1.14) per 1 ug/m3; an IQR increase gave OR 1.64 (no CI, IQR width not stated). Male sex OR 24.71 (5.95-102.54). AUC 0.804. Limitation: 53 events against several trimester windows with no stated multiplicity correction, referral-centre cohort, hernia and hydrocele pooled, and a mechanism inferred rather than tested. Treat as hypothesis. Relevance: low - kriging from fixed stations, with sparse-network error in a trimester-specific contrast, the setting where denser residential estimates would matter.

PAPERS.short: Karimi PMOS polycystic ovary metabolic syndrome Arak Iran PM2.5 PR IDW 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution and polycystic ovary metabolic syndrome (PMOS) in a heavily industrialized Middle Eastern city: A cross-sectional study.
PAPERS.pm: 365-day residential PM2.5 and PM10 by inverse-distance weighting from three stations
PAPERS.affil: Arak University of Medical Sciences, Iran; Arak University of Medical Sciences, Iran
PAPERS.n: 301 women at gynecology clinics in Arak (153 PMOS, 148 non-PMOS), April 2024-March 2025. Modified Poisson, per 1-SD: PM2.5 PR 1.22 (1.09-1.35), PM10 PR 1.23 (1.09-1.36), NO2 1.21 (1.07-1.33), SO2 1.15 (1.01-1.28). Cases had 3.00 ug/m3 more PM2.5. Sensitivity windows and propensity matching agreed. SD widths are not in the abstract. Limitation: exposure from three stations by IDW in an industrial city carries little real spatial contrast, so residence and socioeconomic position are confounded with it; clinic controls and prevalent cases rule out temporal inference. Relevance: moderate - a study whose result hangs on three monitors is where a small low-cost network would directly test the contrast.

PAPERS.short: Qiu stage-specific models pregnancy loss recurrent abortion PM2.5 O3 random forest 2026
PAPERS.title: Stage-Specific Models for Predicting Subsequent Pregnancy Loss in Women with Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion.
PAPERS.pm: Pregnancy-course ambient PM2.5 and O3 metrics as predictors
PAPERS.affil: Peking University, China; Peking University, China
PAPERS.n: Single-centre prospective cohort of 470 women with recurrent spontaneous abortion, 86 (18.3%) with another loss. Three staged models by logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost, repeated 10-fold cross-validation. Third-stage random forest ROC-AUC 0.935 (0.874-0.996); XGBoost 0.870 (0.801-0.938), after adding gestational age, hormones and PM2.5 and O3 metrics. No PM effect estimate. Limitation: internal validation only, 86 events or fewer against many predictors, and gestational age at measurement risks leaking the outcome; the PM contribution cannot be separated from the bundle, and the exposure source is not in the abstract. Relevance: low - PM is a feature in a classifier, and this is no evidence that exposure drives discrimination.

PAPERS.short: Kim district carcinogen emissions thyroid cancer Korea Bayesian PM10 null 2026
PAPERS.title: Association Between District-level Aggregate Carcinogen Emissions and Thyroid Cancer Incidence in Korea: An Ecological Study Using Bayesian Spatial Models.
PAPERS.pm: District PM10 as a covariate; primary exposure a carcinogen release indicator
PAPERS.affil: Seoul National University College of Medicine, South Korea; Seoul National University College of Medicine, South Korea
PAPERS.n: 229 Korean districts, thyroid cancer 2014-2018, Bayesian hierarchical Poisson with mutual adjustment. Aggregate IARC Group 1/2A/2B release indicator RR 1.04 (95% CrI 1.01-1.06) per SD overall, 1.04 (1.02-1.06) in women, 1.02 (0.99-1.06) in men. PM10, NO2, SO2, radon and nuclear-plant proximity showed no association after urban-rural adjustment; CO was inverse (0.96, 0.93-0.99); population density 1.13 (1.06-1.21). Limitation: ecological, and thyroid cancer incidence in Korea is strongly shaped by screening and detection intensity; authors call it hypothesis-generating. PM10 estimate not reported in the abstract. Relevance: low - a coarse-metric null at district scale, informative only in showing that urbanicity adjustment absorbs the PM signal.

PAPERS.short: Zulian urinary chromium nickel welders TIG metalworkers Friuli biomonitoring 2026
PAPERS.title: Biological chromium and nickel monitoring in metalworkers: welders versus non-welders.
PAPERS.pm: Welding fume by job role; urinary Cr and Ni by ICP-MS (no airborne measure)
PAPERS.endpoint: Urinary Cr and Ni, exceedance of ACGIH biological limits
PAPERS.affil: University of Trieste, Italy; University of Trieste, Italy
PAPERS.n: 245 male metalworkers, Friuli Venezia Giulia (179 welders, 66 non-welders), end-of-week urine by ICP-MS. Welders had higher median Cr (0.75 vs 0.56 ug/l, P=0.020) and Ni (1.70 vs 1.10 ug/l, P=0.0001). 50.0% exceeded the Cr limit of 0.7 ug/l. Welding vs non-welding OR 1.71 (0.96-3.06) for exceeding the Cr limit. Age and smoking were unrelated. Limitation: no airborne fume measurement, so job title stands in for exposure, non-welders share the shop air, and the group contrast is correspondingly compressed; Cr speciation not reported. Relevance: low for ambient sensing - a biomarker reference for a workplace aerosol that task-level PM sensors could stratify.

PAPERS.short: Khoshakhlagh occupational airborne pollutants hematological outcomes systematic review 2026
PAPERS.title: Occupational Airborne Pollutant Exposure and Hematological Outcomes in Workplace Settings: A Systematic Review.
PAPERS.pm: Occupational PM, VOCs and heavy metals across 55 studies
PAPERS.affil: Kashan University of Medical Sciences, Iran; AGH University of Krakow, Poland
PAPERS.n: PRISMA review of 1,855 records over five decades, 55 studies, predominantly developing and industrialising countries, JBI appraisal, no pooled estimate. Workplace VOCs, heavy metals such as lead, and PM were linked to subclinical haematological change: lower hemoglobin, altered MCH and MCHC. Linear correlations with pollutant levels were often weak despite high concentrations. BMI associated positively with hemoglobin; age weakly, read as a healthy-worker effect. Limitation: no effect size, PM not separated from co-exposures, and a protective BMI 'buffer' is confounding by nutrition until shown otherwise. Relevance: low - weak exposure-response at high concentrations is also what uncalibrated or area-based workplace exposure metrics would produce.

PAPERS.short: Wu airborne plastics plastic-associated chemicals PM2.5 Singapore PMF I168O 2026
PAPERS.title: Fingerprints of Airborne Plastics in Urban PM2.5: Applications and Implications
PAPERS.pm: Nine plastic-associated chemicals in 240 daily PM2.5 filters, 2018-2020
PAPERS.endpoint: Plastic-associated chemical sources and enrichment within PM2.5
PAPERS.affil: National University of Singapore, Singapore; National University of Singapore, Singapore
PAPERS.n: 240 daily PM2.5 samples, Singapore 2018-2020, nine plastic-associated chemicals, seven apportioned sources. I168O made up 90% of quantified chemicals and identified at least 40% more PM2.5 linked to respirable airborne plastic chemicals. A resolved plastic production, use and burning factor held 37% of quantified chemicals; traffic and road dust held over 20% of near-range chemicals, with DNBP/DEHP above 1 proposed as a non-exhaust marker. Over 90% of DEP sat with transported peat smoke. No uncertainty on factor shares in the abstract. Limitation: one site is implied, and I168O is an additive oxidation product with other potential sources, so the factor measures additives, not plastic mass. Relevance: low for mass sensing - a speciation layer invisible to optical nodes.

PAPERS.short: Gonzalez organosulfates CMAQ hygroscopicity kappa US summers 2013-2022 2026
PAPERS.title: Modeling Decadal Organosulfates in Particulate Matter to Improve Estimations of Aerosol Hygroscopicity in the United States
PAPERS.pm: Isoprene-derived organosulfates and aerosol hygroscopicity from CMAQ, evaluated on IMPROVE
PAPERS.endpoint: Organosulfate concentration and change in hygroscopicity
PAPERS.affil: Texas A&M University, United States; Texas A&M University, United States
PAPERS.n: CMAQ with updated isoprene organosulfate chemistry, contiguous US, summers 2013-2022, evaluated on IMPROVE organosulfur and sulfate plus speciated filters, with an interpretable ML surrogate. Summer mean organosulfate up to 0.51 ug/m3 in the east. Net change in hygroscopicity kappa -5.6% (direct +2.8%, indirect -8.4% through sulfate reduction). No CI on these. Limitation: summer only, isoprene-derived only, and validation rests on sparse speciated measurements; evaluation metrics are not in the abstract. Relevance: moderate - humidity corrections for optical sensors commonly assume a kappa; a chemistry-driven shift of this size, spatially structured, is one physical reason a single continental correction does not transfer.

PAPERS.short: Jiratampradab daily PM2.5 probability distribution upper northern Thailand log-normal 2026
PAPERS.title: Probability Distribution Analysis of Daily PM2.5 Concentration at Five Stations in Upper Northern Thailand
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 at five monitoring stations, June 2023-May 2026
PAPERS.endpoint: Best-fitting distribution and exceedance of the 37.5 ug/m3 standard
PAPERS.affil: King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang, Thailand; Kasetsart University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: 1,096 daily values at each of Chiang Rai, Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Nan and Lampang, June 2023-May 2026. Log-normal, gamma and Weibull fitted by maximum likelihood and compared by Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, AIC and BIC. Log-normal won at all stations. Exceedance of the 24-h 37.5 ug/m3 standard: Nan 25.12%, Lampang 21.70%, Chiang Rai 20.87%. No CI. Limitation: treating strongly autocorrelated, bimodal-season data as independent draws invalidates the goodness-of-fit p-values and understates tail uncertainty, and three years do not constrain extremes. Relevance: low - a descriptive baseline for a haze region where low-cost networks are already dense; useful for setting sensor range and alert thresholds.

PAPERS.short: Cho exercise under particulate matter exposure BDNF neurotrophic narrative review 2026
PAPERS.title: Exercise Under Particulate Matter Exposure: Neurotrophic Responses and Functional Brain Outcomes
PAPERS.pm: Particulate or traffic-related pollution during exercise, heterogeneous metrics
PAPERS.endpoint: BDNF, VEGF, IGF-1, cognitive and brain outcomes
PAPERS.affil: Yonsei University, South Korea; Sun Moon University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Focused narrative review, PubMed and Web of Science, 37 reports (33 main, four indirect). Circulating BDNF responses to exercise under PM were heterogeneous; VEGF and IGF-1 gave complementary peripheral evidence. Human studies mixed attenuation in selected cognitive, dementia and imaging contrasts with retained activity benefit and possible buffering. Central molecular evidence from inhalation was limited; some animal improvements came from intravenous or instillation models. The authors find support for neither a uniform loss of exercise benefit nor a general reversal threshold. No pooling. Limitation: non-systematic, overlapping cohorts possible. Relevance: low-moderate - the stated gap is activity-specific exposure, which is what wearable PM sensing alongside exercise intensity could supply.

PAPERS.short: Wayland discussion data fusion air pollution exposure modeling metadata only 2026
PAPERS.title: Discussion of "Data fusion for air pollution exposure modeling".
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: invited discussion of a data-fusion paper
PAPERS.affil: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Retired), United States; Johns Hopkins University, United States
PAPERS.n: No abstract available from PubMed or Crossref at issue time, and no finding is asserted. PubMed lists this as a discussion at J Air Waste Manag Assoc 76(11):908-916, with authors from the retired EPA, Resources for the Future, Emory and Tennessee among others. Limitation: content unread. Relevance: on title alone high - data fusion is where sensor, monitor, satellite and model fields are combined; retrieve the full text and the paper under discussion.

PAPERS.title: Variability in sources and processes of PM2.5-bound Water Soluble Organic Carbon over an urban location in the North-Western Himalayas
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time

The title places it in PM2.5 water-soluble organic carbon source and process variability at an urban location. Limitation: content unread. Relevance: unknown, retry the abstract at the weekly sweep.

PAPERS.title: Dust storm events in Northeast China by GEOS-Chem modeling and PM measurements
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time

PAPERS.n: Elsevier day-0 deposit, no abstract in Crossref or Semantic Scholar at issue time; no finding is asserted.
